proceduralSpec.proceduralTitle: Data Bus Connector Inspection and Cleaning

proceduralStep.para: Ensure aircraft power is OFF before disconnecting any data bus connectors
Wear ESD wrist strap connected to aircraft ground before handling avionics connectors
Remove connector by grasping connector body, not cable. Pull straight out, do not twist
Inspect connector pins for damage, corrosion, or foreign material using magnification if necessary
If cleaning required, use approved electronic contact cleaner (isopropyl alcohol 99% or approved equivalent)
Allow connector to air dry completely before reconnection (minimum 5 minutes)
Inspect connector receptacle on LRU for damage or foreign material
Align connector carefully and push firmly until fully seated with audible click if applicable
Secure connector locking mechanism (safety wire, locking ring, or retaining clip as applicable)
Verify connector security by gently pulling on cable near connector body

proceduralSpec.proceduralTitle: ARINC 429 Data Bus Testing and Verification

proceduralStep.para: Connect ARINC 429 bus analyzer or test equipment to the data bus under test
Power up aircraft systems and allow minimum 60 seconds for system initialization
Verify transmitter is sending data at correct bit rate (12.5 kbps, 100 kbps, or as specified)
Verify receiver is properly decoding labels and data words
Check signal amplitude: High state 10V ±1V, Low state 0V ±1V (differential measurement)
Verify word parity is correct (odd parity for ARINC 429)
Monitor bus for intermittent errors or missing labels over minimum 5-minute observation period
Document any errors, unexpected labels, or signal quality issues
Connect AFDX test equipment or network analyzer to aircraft Ethernet switch test port
Power up aircraft systems and verify AFDX network initialization
Verify all end systems are present on network using ARP or ICMP ping
Monitor virtual links (VLs) for correct bandwidth allocation groups (BAGs)
Verify no excessive network errors: CRC errors, runt frames, or jabber frames
Check for correct VLAN tagging and priority (QoS) settings on critical data frames
Verify network redundancy by monitoring both Network A and Network B simultaneously
Document network statistics including bandwidth utilization, frame counts, and any anomalies
Verify aircraft power is applied and all relevant circuit breakers are closed
Check data bus connectors are fully seated and locking mechanisms engaged
Verify correct cable routing and no physical damage to cable assemblies
Use bus analyzer to determine if transmitter is sending data
If no transmitter activity, suspect transmitting LRU or upstream power/configuration issue
If transmitter active but receiver not responding, check receiver LRU and downstream wiring
Measure bus termination resistance if applicable (ARINC 429: 75Ω per receiver in parallel)
Isolate fault to cable assembly, connector, or LRU using systematic substitution if necessary
